title: Historical backfill of 2019-2022 legs into partitioned recon tables
subtitle: Spark 3.4 on northstar-batch-eks, 4.6 billion rows, without starving online match
author: Aman Kumar
audience: SE II, data, DBA, and PM deciding how 2019-2022 history lands in recon partitions
owners: Aman Kumar (backfill job), Chris Patel (data), Rina Das (DBA), Priya Nair (EM)
related: CLH-TDD-2023-011, CLH-SOP-2024-011, CLH-PRD-2024-002, CLH-TDD-2023-014, ns-eks-batch-01, CLH-4811
summary: We need 2019-01-02 through 2022-12-30 legs in the partitioned recon tables so Helen Cho can run multi-year break searches and so CLH-PRD-2024-002 replay works on restatements that cite old lots. That is 4.6 billion rows. This design runs Spark 3.4.2 on the dedicated northstar-batch-eks cluster (ns-eks-batch-01), upserts idempotently into recon.leg_raw and recon.leg_break partitions, and is forbidden from touching the OLTP primary as a scan source or as a write target for bulk load. One-off cost is $11.2k. Online match stays on ns-eks-clh-prod-01 and ns-pg-clh-recon-01. The ugly edge is settlement_date timezone for a 2019 DST bug that shifted 41,882 legs by one calendar day.
form_description: Technical design for the 2019-2022 Spark backfill onto partitioned recon tables. Written so we do not run a 4.6 billion row load on the OLTP primary and so the DST edge is explicit before Chris starts the job.
revision_history: First design after Rahul asked for 4-year search in the replay PRD.
Spark plan, partition math, $11.2k cost table.
Approved. DST edge and the rejected OLTP-primary path.

blocks.text: 2019-2022 leg backfill

recon.leg_raw and recon.leg_break are monthly range-partitioned as of CLH-TDD-2023-011. Live traffic writes 2023-01 onward. Everything older lives in Glacier-class Parquet in s3://ns-clh-history-prod/legs/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/ left there by the 2022 warehouse export that Chris Patel ran when we decommissioned the old monolith. Helen cannot query Glacier from Metabase. The replay PRD needs those lots because RailClear restatements in 2024 still cite 2020 allocations for some correspondent 2219 tax-lot arguments. Marcus Bell confirmed with Clearhaven middle office that they will not accept 'history is offline' as an answer after September 2024. So we load it. Once. Into the partitioned tables. With a job that can be killed at 16:50 ET without corrupting 2024 data.

4.6 billion rows is Chris's count from the Parquet footer sums, not a guess. 2019: 0.94B, 2020: 1.12B, 2021: 1.28B, 2022: 1.26B. Average row in Parquet is 184 bytes compressed, 612 bytes reconstructed into the JDBC insert shape. If you run the arithmetic on ns-pg-clh-recon-01 you get a table rewrite that would take the primary for most of a week and would starve match. That is the path this design rejects. Spark on ns-eks-batch-01 writes to a side cluster ns-pg-clh-recon-bulk-01, we attach partitions, we swap. Details below.
Decision

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Run the backfill on northstar-batch-eks with Spark 3.4.2. Source is the Parquet history bucket. Writes go to ns-pg-clh-recon-bulk-01, then partitions ATTACH to the prod primary during a Saturday freeze window with Rina Das. Do not SELECT 4.6B rows out of the OLTP primary. Do not COPY into the primary. Do not run Spark executors in clearhaven-prod. Budget $11.2k one-off, already socialized with Priya Nair. Idempotent upsert key is (leg_id, source_system, as_of_ts). Settlement_date is stored as date in America/New_York with an explicit dst_shift_2019 flag for the 41,882 rows the 2019 bug touched.

Rahul Deshmukh asked whether we could just raise the primary to r6i.8xlarge for two weeks and load in place. Rina Das said no on 2024-07-11, in the meeting, out loud, so it would be in the notes. The primary already sits at 61.4% cache hit for the hot partitions during month-end and 12-40s write stalls when autovacuum loses. A 4.6B row COPY would finish autovacuum as a product. We are not doing that.
Constraints

items: Online match on ns-eks-clh-prod-01 must not see CPU steal, Kafka consumer lag, or Postgres write latency over 40ms p95 attributable to the backfill. Diego Alvarez will page us if p95 goes over 40ms for 5 minutes.
The job must be idempotent. A kill at 60% and a restart must not duplicate legs. Helen's count distinct on leg_id is the audit.

2019-2022 data is financial history. Same handling as live: no dumps to laptops, no sample CSVs in Slack. Spark event logs go to the encrypted history bucket, not to a public Spark UI on the internet.
Must finish before 2024-09-20 so Helen has a month of practice queries before the September month-end that the capacity memo cares about.
Cost cap $12.5k. Estimate is $11.2k. If we cross $12.5k we stop and replan, we do not quietly keep the cluster up over a weekend.
Rina approves every ATTACH PARTITION. Aman does not run ATTACH on a Saturday morning alone.

blocks.text: Why not the OLTP primary

ns-pg-clh-recon-01 is the source of truth for live match. It is also a single writer with 16 vCPU and 128Gi RAM, already doing month-end at 8.2M files/day class. A Spark JDBC read of 4.6B rows from that box would take sequential scans on toasted XML (yes, some 2019 rows still have the XML blob in-row from the monolith). Chris tried a 10-million-row probe on 2024-07-08 against a snapshot restored to the bulk cluster, not against prod, and saw 14.6 minutes. Linear scaling is a lie because of XML toast, but even a friendly 400x is days of scan. A JDBC write of 4.6B rows into the live tables would generate WAL that ships to the sync replica, fill the 4TB data volume (we have 2.14TB free of 8TB, and the reconstructed 4.6B is about 2.62TB before indexes), and trip the disk alarm Diego already watches. We would also block CLH-SOP-2024-011 migrations for a week. Rejected.

The other rejected variant was logical replication from a restored 2019 snapshot of the old monolith's Postgres into prod. The monolith schema does not match recon.leg_raw. We would write a converter anyway, and the snapshot restore still needs a cluster. That converter is Spark. Skip the extra replica and start with Parquet, which already exists and is the file Chris checksummed.
Cluster: northstar-batch-eks

ns-eks-batch-01 is the dedicated EMR-shaped cluster we already use for the overnight RailClear splitter scale tests. Kubernetes 1.28, Spark operator 3.4.2, node group batch-r6id.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 122Gi, 1x800Gi NVMe). We will run a SparkApplication named clh-leg-history-backfill with 1 driver (4 vCPU, 16Gi) and 24 executors (4 vCPU, 28Gi, 2 cores each in Spark terms). That is 96 executor cores. The node group autoscale max is 32 nodes; we will cap this job at 8 nodes so the overnight splitter tests still have room. Priya confirmed the cap with the platform team on 2024-07-18.

The Spark UI is only reachable from ops-bastion-03 via the internal ALB spark-ui.batch.northstar.internal. Do not poke a hole. Event logs: s3://ns-clh-history-prod/spark-events/clh-leg-history-backfill/. Diego will delete them after 90 days.

blocks.text: Write path and idempotent upserts

We do not INSERT blindly. 2019-2022 history was exported twice (January 2023 and a repair in March 2023 after Chris found 0.18% duplicate footers). The Parquet can contain two copies of a leg with the same leg_id and different as_of_ts. Live 2023+ data must win if a key collides, which it should not, but the 2019 DST bug produced re-issued legs with new ids and old settlement_dates, so we will see near-collisions. The upsert key is (leg_id, source_system, as_of_ts). We keep the row with the max as_of_ts. We never update a row whose load_batch_id starts with live-. That guard is a WHERE clause on the bulk table and a trigger on prod that Rina will install before ATTACH, then drop after we confirm no live key sits in a 2019 partition (there should not be one).

Implementation: Spark writes Parquet shuffled by month to s3://ns-clh-history-prod/legs-load/dt=YYYY-MM/, then a per-month JDBC job COPY's into recon.leg_raw_2019_01 etc on the bulk cluster using ON CONFLICT (leg_id, source_system, as_of_ts) DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE recon.leg_raw.as_of_ts < EXCLUDED.as_of_ts. Postgres 14 supports that predicate. Batch size 5,000 rows per COPY stream, 8 streams per month table, which is how we stay under the bulk cluster's 12000 IOPS. Chris measured 41.2k rows/s on a 20M-row rehearsal. At 41.2k, 4.6B is 31.0 hours of COPY if perfectly serial. We run 4 months in parallel on 4 JDBC writers, so wall clock COPY is about 8.2 hours plus Spark shuffle 6.4 hours plus retries. Plan for 22 hours of cluster uptime across two weeknights and a Saturday ATTACH.

-- target DDL on ns-pg-clh-recon-bulk-01 (Rina runs this, not Spark)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recon.leg_raw_2019_01
  (LIKE recon.leg_raw INCLUDING DEFAULTS INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS);

ALTER TABLE recon.leg_raw_2019_01
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_leg_raw_2019_01_range
  CHECK (trade_date >= DATE '2019-01-01' AND trade_date < DATE '2019-02-01');

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_leg_raw_2019_01_id
  ON recon.leg_raw_2019_01 (leg_id, source_system, as_of_ts);

-- upsert shape used by the JDBC writer
-- INSERT INTO recon.leg_raw_2019_01 AS t (...)
-- VALUES (...)
-- ON CONFLICT (leg_id, source_system, as_of_ts)
-- DO UPDATE SET
--   qty = EXCLUDED.qty,
--   settlement_date = EXCLUDED.settlement_date,
--   dst_shift_2019 = EXCLUDED.dst_shift_2019,
--   load_batch_id = EXCLUDED.load_batch_id

blocks.text: Spark job sketch

# spark-submit shape. Operator YAML is in deploy/batch/clh-leg-history-backfill.yaml
# Do not run this on ns-eks-clh-prod-01.

spark-submit \
  --master k8s://https://ns-eks-batch-01.northstar.internal \
  --deploy-mode cluster \
  --name clh-leg-history-backfill \
  --conf spark.kubernetes.namespace=clearhaven-batch \
  --conf spark.kubernetes.container.image=111111111111.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ns-clh/leg-backfill:0.6.1 \
  --conf spark.executor.instances=24 \
  --conf spark.executor.cores=2 \
  --conf spark.executor.memory=24g \
  --conf spark.driver.memory=12g \
  --conf spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=672 \
  --conf spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.aws.credentials.provider=com.amazonaws.auth.WebIdentityTokenCredentialsProvider \
  --class com.northstar.clearhaven.backfill.LegHistoryJob \
  local:///opt/ns/leg-backfill.jar \
  --src s3a://ns-clh-history-prod/legs/ \
  --dst s3a://ns-clh-history-prod/legs-load/ \
  --start 2019-01-02 \
  --end 2022-12-30 \
  --tz America/New_York \
  --dst-shift-file s3a://ns-clh-history-prod/fixes/dst_shift_2019_ids.parquet
blocks.caption: Submit is via the operator in practice. The flags are the contract. --tz America/New_York is mandatory; UTC default is the 2019 bug all over again.

blocks.text: Edge: settlement_date and the 2019 DST bug

In March 2019 the monolith stored settlement_date as a timestamp without time zone, defaulted to the JVM's zone, which on the old app hosts was UTC. Clearhaven ops, then and now, mean settlement_date as a New York calendar date. On 2019-03-10 (US spring forward) a settlement timestamp of 2019-03-10 00:20:00 UTC was stored, and when someone later CAST it to date in New York they got 2019-03-09. The reverse happened in November. Chris's 2023 export wrote date(settlement_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') in one path and date(settlement_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') in another, depending on which exporter version ran that night. We have 41,882 legs where the two methods disagree by one day. Helen has a printed list of 200 of them from a 2020 audit. Marcus says Clearhaven's official date is the New York calendar date on the trade confirm, not the UTC date.

The backfill will apply a fix file dst_shift_2019_ids.parquet (41,882 ids, plus the confirmed New York date from the 2020 audit extract we still have in the history bucket). Rows in the fix file get settlement_date from the file and dst_shift_2019 = true. Rows not in the file get settlement_date = date(settlement_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') and dst_shift_2019 = false. We will not guess. If a row has a null settlement_ts, we leave settlement_date null and emit a counter. Nulls in 2019 are 2,144 rows in the Parquet, mostly cancelled pre-allocations. Helen said leave them null, do not invent a date.

If we skip the fix file, multi-year searches that filter settlement_date = 2019-03-11 will miss about 6,400 legs that Clearhaven still thinks settled that day. Replay of those lots would also miss. This is the class of bug that looks like a 0.0009% data issue and then eats a week of ops time. The fix file is part of the job contract. A run without --dst-shift-file is a failed run even if row counts match 4.6B.

blocks.text: Not starving online match

Isolation is the actual design. Spark has no network path to ns-pg-clh-recon-01. The bulk cluster's security group allows 5432 from ns-eks-batch-01 only. Prod primary allows 5432 from match-engine, break-svc, and Rina's DBA jump, not from batch. Diego already opened CLH-4811 to add a deny rule so a future well-meaning JDBC URL cannot point at prod. The Saturday ATTACH is the one moment prod feels this job. ATTACH PARTITION in Postgres 14 is a metadata lock. Rina's last ATTACH on a similar-sized table (not 4.6B, a 90M archive) took 1.8 seconds when no one was running a long transaction. If match-engine has a 30-second transaction open on the parent table, ATTACH waits. So we ATTACH at 10:15 ET Saturday, after Helen confirms unmatched is under 1,200, and we ask match-engine owners (me) to avoid ad-hoc ANALYZE. The freeze window in CLH-SOP-2024-011 already covers this.

During weeknight Spark runs, the risk to prod is not Postgres, it is AWS noise: NAT, S3, ECR pull. We pull images once and pin. S3 is the history bucket, not the inbound landing bucket match-engine uses. If someone copies the history job to read s3://ns-clh-inbound-prod/ you will compete with live ingest. Do not. Chris's IAM role ns-clh-backfill-job can read history and write legs-load, and cannot list inbound.

blocks.text: Cost

The $11.2k figure is Chris's spreadsheet from 2024-07-16, not a round $10k. It assumes 22 hours of 8 x r6id.4xlarge on-demand ($2.4192/hour each in us-east-1 on our EDP, so $425.8 for nodes), 8TB gp3 on the bulk cluster for 14 days ($1,126.4 for the extra volume and IOPS above the idle bulk box), Spark shuffle S3 PUT/GET on 2.1TB of intermediate data ($184.6), JDBC idle on bulk Postgres instance already in the bill at $0 incremental if we finish in the 14-day window we already pay for, and 40 hours of people time at the internal loaded rate Finance told Priya to use ($9,440). The people line is most of it. If you tell Finance the cluster is $11.2k they will think we bought a boat. Show them the split.

blocks.text: Rejected cost-saving idea: use spot executors. We tried spot on a 20M rehearsal. 3 of 24 executors vanished mid-shuffle and the stage reran for 41 minutes. Fine for rehearsal. Not fine when Rina is waiting on a Saturday ATTACH slot that we asked Helen to keep clear. On-demand for this job. Spot for the next one if we ever backfill 2016-2018, which we should not promise.
Schedule

items: 2024-07-24 to 2024-07-26: Rina creates monthly partition shells on bulk for 2019-01 through 2022-12. Aman reviews names against prod parent tables.
2024-07-29 weeknight: Spark shuffle 2019 only. JDBC load 2019_01 through 2019_03 as a canary. Helen samples 200 ids including 40 from the DST fix file.
2024-07-30: if canary matches, Spark shuffle the rest. Do not JDBC all months yet.
2024-08-01 to 2024-08-08: JDBC remaining months, four at a time, off the 17:00-20:30 ET freeze even though this is not prod. Habit.
2024-08-10 Saturday 10:15 ET: ATTACH 2019. Stop. Helen queries. If wrong, DETACH (Rina), do not drop.
2024-08-17 Saturday: ATTACH 2020-2022 in three batches with 20-minute pauses. Diego watches prod p95.
2024-08-20: drop bulk volume or snapshot it for 30 days. Chris writes the row-count certificate.
2024-09-20: hard deadline for Helen's practice. If we miss 2024-08-17, slip ATTACH, do not rush a Thursday night ATTACH.

blocks.text: Rejected alternatives
Load on the OLTP primary. Died 2024-07-11. Disk, WAL, autovacuum, freeze calendar, and Rina. See above.

Athena over the Parquet for Helen, skip the load. Rahul floated it because $11.2k buys a lot of Athena. Died 2024-07-15. Replay (CLH-PRD-2024-002) needs the legs in recon.leg_raw so match-engine can see them with the same SQL as live. Athena cannot be a foreign table we join in the 7:20 path. Also Athena plus Glacier restore latency is 4-12 minutes on the cold prefixes, which Helen will not sit through. We can keep Athena for ad-hoc, and we will, but it is not the backfill.

Dump Parquet into Kafka and let match-engine consume 4.6B historical records. Kavya estimated 14 days of consumer time even with a dedicated consumer group, and it would fight the live topic's disk (see the FY25 capacity memo). It would also re-run matching logic on 2019 breaks that ops already closed. Helen does not want 2019 breaks reopening in her 2024 queue. The backfill loads facts. It does not re-match. Closed breaks stay closed; we load recon.leg_break with status = HISTORICAL_CLOSED and a filter so the live queue ignores them.
What HISTORICAL_CLOSED means for ops

Every 2019-2022 break row gets status HISTORICAL_CLOSED and break_code_v2 copied from whatever the monolith had, mapped through recon.break_code_map when we can. Live dashboards filter status not in (HISTORICAL_CLOSED). Helen's multi-year search will have a toggle. Default off. If we forget the filter, the 7:20 queue becomes a museum. Sneha Iyer has a test that a live queue query returns 0 historical rows on a fixture. That test is required to merge the ATTACH-day application flag.
